Notes: The Desktop's DesktopCaptureRunner runs unchanged but for its options: this tool as its broker over a qualification root, never the production root; a session root in the output directory; the run's length as the capture's quota, which the broker ends it at; and the window it keeps, as the Explore card's rolling choices ask for it.
Traffic is one paced loopback TCP stream (1 KiB every 20 ms) plus a new connection each second, on top of whatever else the machine did during the run.

Each sample reads the latest overview the runner handed over: its rows, the session time its extent spans (what it holds), where the session keeps every record from and the rows it kept from before as identity evidence. It sums the bytes of the session's files and of the capture's evidence, counts the journal chunks each holds, and reads the viewer's private bytes and managed heap, the latter as of its latest collection, and the broker's private bytes.

Judged are the samples taken while recording from the window and its slack plus a minute on, by when the session's first release is due. The window is held when the session's extent spans no less than the window less 30 s and no more than the window, its slack and 30 s, at every judged sample, at the end and in the saved session reopened. What each has given up is the capture's chunks it was given - published by the broker, derived by the follow - less the journal chunks its files hold. The evidence keeps no more than the session when, at every judged sample, it has given up all the session had at the sample before, less 3 chunks for the counts' moments: the broker releases what the session gave up once the runner's next lease renewal says so. Bounded means the median of the judged samples' last quarter is within 1.5 times their first quarter's, for the session's bytes per row and the evidence's, so the rate of the machine's traffic cancels out, and for the viewer's heap.
A run under DOTNET_GCHeapHardLimit with a wide DOTNET_GCRegionRange, as the report names, also shows the viewer kept within that heap for its whole length: otherwise it runs out of memory and fails.

A load of 1,400 messages a second ran beside that traffic for the whole recording: a second loopback TCP stream writing 1 KiB messages in bursts every 20 ms, each read at its other end before the next, so a window holds as many rows as a busy machine's whatever else the machine did; the messages it sent are counted.
FinalDetail: The configured maximum capture duration elapsed; evidence was finalized.
